translations.text: I made this first account, O lover of God, about all that Jesus began to do and to teach,
until the day of his ascension, when he gave commands through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom he had chosen, and he was taken up,
to whom he also presented himself alive after his suffering in many ways. For forty days he appeared to them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God.
He stayed with them and commanded them: "Do not leave Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father, which you heard from me.
For John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days after these."
Those who had gathered asked him, saying: "Lord, will you at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?"
He said to them: "It is not for you to know the times or the years, which the Father has set by his own authority;
but you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth."
And when he had said this, while they were still watching, he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight.
And while they were still standing and gazing into heaven at his ascension, behold, two men in white garments stood over them,
who said to them: "Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking toward heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him taken up into heaven."
Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mountain called the Mount of Olives, which is near Jerusalem, about a Sabbath day's journey away.

And when they had entered the city, they went up to the upper room where Peter and John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James were staying.
All these were devoting themselves together to prayer, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brothers.
In those days Peter stood up among the disciples and spoke; the crowd numbered in all about a hundred and twenty people:
"Men, it was necessary for this scripture to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand through the mouth of David about Judas, who became the guide of those who seized Jesus,
for he was counted among us and had been allotted a share in this ministry and apostleship.
This man acquired the field with the wages of falsehood, and he swelled up and burst open in the middle, and all his entrails poured out.
And this became known to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the field was even called in their own language Akeldama, that is, Field of Blood.
For it is written in the Book of Psalms: 'Let his dwelling be desolate, and let there be no one living in it'; and 'Let another take his office.'
Therefore, of these men who have gathered with us all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,
beginning from the baptism of John until the day of his ascension from us, one of these must become a witness of his resurrection with us."
And they put forward two: Joseph, who was called Barsabbas and was also named Justus, and Matthias.
And they prayed and said: "You, Lord, who know all hearts, show which one of these two
to receive the share of the ministry from which Judas turned aside to go to his own place."
And they cast lots for them, and the lot fell upon Matthias, and he was counted with the eleven apostles as the twelfth.
And when that day of Pentecost had come, they were all gathered together with one another,
and suddenly there came from heaven a roaring, like the rush of a violent wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting;
and there appeared to them divided tongues as of fire, and it rested upon each one of them.
And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak in foreign tongues, as the Spirit gave them to speak.
There were Jews living in Jerusalem, God-fearing men from every nation that is under heaven.
And when this sound came, the crowd of people gathered and was bewildered, because each one of them heard his own language when they spoke.
They were all astonished and amazed, and said to one another: "Look, are not all these who are speaking Galileans?
And how is it that each of us hears his own language, we who are:
Persians and Uzhiks [?] and Elamites, and those who live in Mesopotamia and in Judea and in Cappadocia, in Pontus and Asia,
in Phrygia and Pamphylia, in Egypt and the parts of the region of Libya toward Cyrene, and visitors from Rome,
Jews and proselytes, Cretans and Arabians — we hear them speaking in our own tongues these riches of God."
They were all amazed, one with another, and said: "What do these men mean to do?"
But others mocked them and said, "They are full of sweet wine."
Peter stood up among the eleven, raised his voice, and said to them: "Men of Judea, and all who live in Jerusalem, let this be known among you, and listen to my words.
For these men are not drunk, as you suppose, since it is only the third hour of the day.
But this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel:

'And it shall be after this, says the Lord God, that I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and to your old men it shall be revealed in dreams;
and upon my menservants and maidservants in those days [?] of my Spirit, and they shall prophesy.
And I will give signs in the heavens and wonders on the earth: blood and fire and a vapour of smoke;
the sun shall be turned to darkness and the moon to blood, before the coming of that great and appointed day of the Lord.
And it shall be that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.'
Men of Israel, hear my words. This Jesus of Nazareth, a man appointed by God for you through mighty works and signs and wonders, which God did through him among you, as you yourselves know —
this man, by the set purpose and foreknowledge of God, handed over by the hands of lawless men, you nailed to the cross and killed,
whom God raised up, and loosed the pangs of death, because it was not possible for him to be held by it.
For David says concerning him: "I foresaw the Lord, he is before me always, for he is at my right hand [?], so that I may not be shaken;
therefore my heart was glad and my tongue rejoiced all the more, and my flesh also shall dwell in hope.
For you will not leave my soul in hell, nor will you give your holy one to see corruption;
you have made known to me, O Lord, your ways of life, and you will fill me with joy by your countenance."
Men, brothers, it is right to speak openly to you about the patriarch David: he died and was buried, and his tomb is among us to this very day.
He was a prophet and knew that God had sworn to him with an oath to raise up the Christ from the fruit of his womb and to seat him on his thrones.
He foretold and spoke of the resurrection of Christ, that his soul was not left in hell, nor did his flesh see corruption.
This Jesus God raised up, of which we are all witnesses;
he was exalted by the right hand of God, and having received the promise of the Spirit from the Father, he has poured out this which you see and hear.
For David did not ascend into heaven; he himself says: "The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand,
until I put your enemies beneath your feet."
Let all the house of Israel know assuredly that God has made him Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified."
When they heard this, they repented in their hearts and said to Peter and the other apostles: "And what shall we do, men, brothers?"
And Peter said to them: "Repent, and let each one of you be baptized in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you shall receive the promise of the Holy Spirit;
for the promise is yours and your children's and of all who are far off, whomever the Lord our God calls."
And with many other words he testified, entreated them, and said: "Be saved from this crooked generation."
And they joyfully received his word, and on that day about three thousand were baptized.
And they were devoted to the teaching of the apostles, and to communion, and to the blessing, and to prayer.
Fear was upon every soul; many signs and wonders were done by the apostles in Jerusalem; great fear was upon them all.
All the believers were together and had everything in common;
they sold their fields and possessions and distributed it to all, as anyone had need.
Day by day they were devoted in the temple, they blessed bread from house to house, and took food with glad and simple heart;
they praised God and had favour with all the people.
And the Lord added more of those being saved to the church day by day.
Peter and John were going up to the temple at the very hour of prayer, the ninth hour.
And there was a certain man, lame from his mother's womb, whom they used to carry and set down day by day at the doors of the temple called Beautiful, to ask alms from those going into the temple.
When he saw Peter and John about to go into the temple, he asked them for alms.
Peter, together with John, looked at him and said, "Look at us."
And he looked at them, expecting to receive something from them.
Peter said to him, "Gold and silver we do not have; but what we have, we give to you: in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, rise up and walk!"
And he took him by his right hand and raised him up. At once his feet and ankles were made strong.
And he stood up and walked, and went into the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God.
And all the people saw him walking and praising God.
They recognized him as the one who used to sit for alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple. And they were filled with fear and amazement at what had happened to him.
And as he was holding on to Peter and John, all the people gathered to them in the portico called Solomon's, because of the wonder.
When Peter saw this, he said to the people: "Men of Israel, why are you amazed at this? Or why do you look at us, as though by our own power or piety we had made this man walk?
The God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified his son Jesus, whom you handed over and denied before Pilate, who had decided to release him.
But you denied the Holy and Righteous One, and asked for a murderer instead.
And you killed the Author of life, whom God raised from the dead; of this we are witnesses.
And through faith in his name, his name has made strong this man whom you see and know; and the faith that comes through him has given him this soundness of life before you all.
And now we know, brothers, that you acted in ignorance, as did your rulers.
But what God foretold through the mouth of all his prophets, that his Christ would suffer, he has fulfilled in this way.
Now therefore repent and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped away,
so that, when the times of refreshing come from the presence of the Lord, he may send the one on whom you laid hands, Christ Jesus,
whom heaven must receive until the time of the restoration of all things, of which God spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets.
Moses said: "The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brothers, like me; listen to him in everything he tells you.
And it shall be that every soul that does not listen to that prophet, that soul shall be destroyed from among his people."
And all the prophets from Samuel and those who came after him, as many as spoke, also foretold these days.
For you are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant which God promised to your fathers, saying to Abraham: "In your offspring all the families of the earth shall be blessed."
To you first God raised up his Son Jesus and sent him to bless you, so that each one of you may turn away from your wickedness."
And as they were speaking to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them,
angered because they were teaching the people and proclaiming through Jesus the resurrection of the dead.
And they laid their hands on them and put them in custody until the next day, for it was already evening.
And many of those who heard their word believed. And the number of the men who believed came to about five thousand.
And on the next day their rulers, elders and scribes gathered together in Jerusalem,
with Annas the high priest and Caiaphas and John and Alexander, and as many as were of the high priests' family.
And they set them in their midst and asked them: "By what power or by what name have you done this?"
Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them: "Rulers of the people and elders of Israel,
if we are being examined today concerning a good deed done to a sick man, as to how this man was healed,
let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead, by him this man stands before you alive.
This is the stone that was despised by you, the builders, which has become the head of the corner. And there is salvation in no one else,
nor is there any other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved."
Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and of John, and knew that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they were amazed; and they recognized that they had been with Jesus.
And seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, they could say nothing against it.
And they ordered them to go out of the council; they spoke to one another
and said: "What shall we do to these men? For a sign has plainly been done through them, [evident] to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem [?], and we cannot deny it.
But so that it may spread no further among the people, let us threaten them that they speak to no one in this name."
And they called them and commanded them: "Do not speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus."
But Peter and John answered and said to them: "Whether it is right before God to listen to you rather than to God, you judge.
For we cannot help speaking of what we have seen and heard."
And when they had threatened them further, they let them go, finding no way to punish them, because of the people, for all were glorifying God for what had happened.
For the man on whom this sign of healing had been performed was more than forty years old.
When they had been released, they went to their own people and reported what the high priests and the elders had said to them.
And when they heard this, they lifted up their voices to God together and said: "Lord, you are God, who made heaven and earth and everything in them,
You who through our father, by the Holy Spirit, by the mouth of David your servant, said: "Why did the nations rage, and the people plot vain things?
The kings of the earth came, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against his Anointed."
For truly they gathered together in this holy city against your holy Son Jesus, whom you anointed: Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the nations, together with the people of Israel,
to do whatever your hand and your counsel had determined beforehand should be done.
And now, Lord, look upon their threats, and grant to your servants to speak your word with all boldness,
while you stretch out your hand to heal and to perform signs and wonders through the name of your holy Son Jesus."
And as they prayed, the place where they were gathered was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God boldly.
Now the multitude of those who believed were of one heart and one mind, and not one of them said that any of his possessions was his own, but they had everything in common.
And with great power the apostles gave their testimony to the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ, and great grace was upon them all.
No one among them was in need, and those who were owners of lands or houses sold them and brought the proceeds of what they sold,
and laid it at the apostles' feet, and it was distributed to each one as anyone had need.
And Joseph, who was called Barnabas by the apostles, which means son of consolation, a Levite, a Cypriot by birth,
sold a field, brought the price, and laid it at the apostles' feet.
A certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a piece of land,
and he kept back part of the price, and his wife also knew of it, and he brought only a certain part and laid it at the apostles' feet.
Peter said to him: "Ananias, why has the devil filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and to keep back part of the price of the land?
While it remained, was it not yours? And after it was sold, was it not still in your own power? Why have you set this deed in your heart? You have not lied to men, but to God."
When Ananias heard these words, he fell down and breathed his last. And great fear came upon all who heard of it.
The young men rose up, wrapped him, carried him out, and buried him.
About three hours later, when his wife did not know what had happened, she came in.
Peter said to her: "Tell me, did you sell the land for so much?" And she said: "Yes, for so much."
Peter said to her: "Why have you agreed together to test the Holy Spirit? Look, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out too."
Immediately she fell down at his feet and breathed her last. The young men came in, found her dead, carried her out, and buried her beside her husband.
And great fear came upon the whole church and upon all who heard of these things.
Through the hands of the apostles many signs were done among the people, and they were all together in Solomon's Portico.
But the others could not join them, yet the people praised them highly.
And all the more a multitude of men and women who believed in the Lord was added,
so that they even carried the sick out into the streets and laid them on beds and stretchers, so that when Peter came by, at least his shadow might fall on some of them.
And a multitude from the surrounding cities gathered to Jerusalem, and they brought the sick and those troubled by unclean spirits, and all of them were healed.
The high priest rose up, and all who were with him, that is, the sect of the Sadducees, and they were filled with jealousy;
and they laid their hands on the apostles and put them in prison, to be held in public custody.
But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison, brought them out, and said:
"Go, stand in the temple, and speak to the people all the words of this life."

When they heard this, they went into the temple just at dawn and taught the people. Then the high priest and those with him came and called together the council and all the elders of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison to have the apostles brought.
But when the servants went there, they did not find them in the prison. They came back and reported to them,
saying: "We found the prison locked with all security and the guards standing in front of the doors. But when we opened it, we found no one inside."
When the captain of the temple and the high priests heard these words, they were puzzled about them, wondering what this could be.
Then someone came and told them: "The men whom you put in prison are in the temple, standing and teaching the people."
Then the captain went with the servants and brought them, but not by force, because he was afraid that the people might stone them.
He brought them and stood them in the middle of the council. The high priest questioned them
and said: "We strictly commanded you not to teach in this name. And now, look, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you mean to bring this man's blood upon us."
Peter and the apostles answered and said: "We must obey God rather than men.
The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, on whom you laid hands and whom you hanged on a tree.
God exalted him with his right hand as leader and savior, to give Israel repentance and the forgiveness of sins.
And we are his witnesses to these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him."
When they heard this, they were cut to the quick with rage and plotted to kill them.
But a Pharisee in the council stood up, named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law who was honored among the people, and he ordered the men to be taken outside;
and he said to them: "Men of Israel, be careful about what you intend to do to these men.
For some time ago Theudas rose up, claiming to be somebody, and about four hundred men followed him. He too was destroyed, and all his followers were broken up and came to nothing.
After him Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the census and led many people away to follow him. He too perished, and all his followers were scattered.
"And now I tell you, keep away from these men and let them go. If this word or this work is from men, it will be overthrown;
but if it is from God, you will not be able to overthrow them, or you may even be found fighting against God." And they obeyed him.
And they called in the apostles, beat them, and commanded them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.
And they went away from the council rejoicing, because they had been counted worthy to suffer dishonor for his name.
And every day they were in the temple, and they did not cease from teaching and preaching the gospel of Jesus Christ.
In those days, as the disciples were multiplying, there arose a murmuring of the Greeks against the Hebrews, because their widows were being neglected in the daily ministration.
Then the twelve called the multitude of the disciples together and said to them: "It is not fitting for us to leave the word of God and serve tables.
Brothers, choose from among you seven men of good report, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this need.
But we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word."

And the word pleased the whole multitude, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip and Prochorus and Nicanor and Timon and Parmenas and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch.
And they prayed and laid their hands on them.
And the word of the Lord grew, and the number of the disciples in Jerusalem multiplied greatly [?] in the faith.
And Stephen was full of the Holy Spirit and of power, and he worked signs and wonders among the great people.

Then some men rose up from the synagogue which was called that of the Libertines, and of those from Cilicia and from Asia, and of the Cyrenians and of the Alexandrians, and they disputed with Stephen,
and they could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.
Then they secretly induced certain men, who said: "We heard him speaking words of blasphemy against Moses and against God."
They stirred up the people and the elders and the scribes, and they came upon him, seized him, and brought him before the council.
And they set up false witnesses, who said: "This man does not cease speaking evil words against this holy place and the law;
for we heard him say that Jesus the Nazarene will destroy this place and change the law which Moses gave us."
And all who sat there in the council looked at him and saw his face like the face of an angel.
The high priest said to him: "Are these things so?"
And he said: "Men, brothers and fathers, hear me. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he settled in Haran,
and said to him: 'Go out from your land and from your kindred into the land that I will show you.'
Then he went out from the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran. Then, after the death of his father, he came to this land in which you now dwell;
and he gave him no inheritance in it, not even a place to set his foot, and he promised to give it to him as a possession, and to his descendants. And he had no child.
God said to him: "Your descendants will be sojourners in a foreign land, and they will enslave them and mistreat them for four hundred years.
And I will judge the nation which they serve," said the Lord, "and after this they will come out and worship me in this place."
And he gave him the covenant of circumcision. And so he fathered Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.
And the patriarchs were jealous of Joseph and sold him into Egypt, and God was with him,
and rescued him from all his afflictions and gave him favour and wisdom before Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians. And he appointed him ruler over Egypt and over all his house.
There was a famine in Egypt and in Canaan, and great affliction, and our fathers could not find food.
When Jacob heard that there was food in Egypt, he sent our fathers out the first time,
and on the second visit Joseph made himself known to his brothers, and Joseph's family became known to Pharaoh's house.
Joseph sent and summoned his father Jacob and all his kindred, seventy-five souls.
And Jacob went down to Egypt, and he died, he and our fathers.
And they were carried to Shechem and buried in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
And as the time of the promise drew near which God had promised to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,
until another king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.
He dealt oppressively with our people and mistreated our fathers, and made them cast out their infants so that they would not survive.
At this time Moses was born, and he was beautiful before God; he was brought up for three months in his father's house.
And when he was cast out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and brought him up as her own son.
And Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians; he was mighty in words and deeds.
And when forty years of his life were being completed, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the sons of Israel,
and he saw someone being wronged; he intervened against the one doing the harm, avenged the one who was wronged, and killed the Egyptian.
He supposed that his brothers would understand that God was giving them salvation by his hand, but they did not understand.
The next day he appeared to them as they were quarrelling and tried to reconcile them in peace, and he said to them: "Men, you are brothers: why do you wrong one another?"
But the one who was wronging his neighbour pushed him away and said: "Who appointed you ruler and judge over us?
Or do you want to kill me, as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?"
And at this word Moses fled, and he became a sojourner in the land of Midian, where he had two sons.
And when forty years had been completed, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai in a flame of fire in a bush;
Moses was amazed when he saw the vision, and as he went up to look at it, the voice of the Lord came:
"I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob." Moses trembled and did not dare to look.
The Lord said to him: "Take the sandals off your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.
I have truly seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to rescue them. Now come, I will send you to Egypt."
This Moses they had rejected, saying, "Who made you ruler and judge over us?" Yet God sent this man as ruler and deliverer by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
He led them out, and he did wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, at the Red Sea and in the wilderness for forty years.
This is the Moses who said to the children of Israel: "The Lord God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brothers, like me; listen to him."
This is the one who was with the people in the wilderness, with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers. He received living words to give to you.
Your fathers refused to obey him. Instead they pushed him away, and in their hearts they turned back to the land of Egypt.
They said to Aaron: "Make us gods who will go before us. As for Moses, who led us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him."
In those days they set up the calf, offered sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the work of their hands.

God turned away and gave them over to serve the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: "Did you offer me slain beasts and sacrifices for forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
You took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, the idols that you made in order to worship them. So I will remove you beyond Babylon."
Our fathers had the tent of witness with them in the wilderness. It was made as the one who spoke to Moses commanded: he was to make it according to the pattern he had seen.

Our fathers received it in turn and brought it in with Joshua when they took possession of the land of the nations. God drove those nations out before our fathers. So it remained until the days of David,
who found favor before God and asked to find a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
But it was Solomon who built him a house.
Yet the Most High does not dwell in temples made by hands, as the prophet said:
"Heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool of my feet. What kind of house will you build for me, says the Lord, or what place will be my resting place?
Did not my hand make all these things?"
You hard-hearted and stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in heart and ears! You always rise up against the Holy Spirit and resist him. You are just like your fathers.
Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? They killed those who foretold the coming of the Holy One, and now you have become his betrayers and murderers,
you who received the law by the ordinance of angels and did not keep it."
When they heard this, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed their teeth at him.
But he was full of faith and of the Holy Spirit. He looked up to heaven and saw the glory of the Lord, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
And he said, "Behold, look, I see the heavens opened and the Son of God standing at the right hand of God."
They cried out with a loud voice, stopped their ears, and rushed upon him,
and they took him outside the city and began stoning him. And those who were the killers took off their garments and laid them at the feet of a certain young man whose name was Saul.
And they were stoning Stephen, and he was crying out and saying, "Lord, receive my spirit."
He knelt down, cried out, and said with a loud voice, "Lord, do not hold this sin against them." And when he had said this, he fell asleep.

This Saul was consenting to his killing. In those days there was a great persecution against the church that was in Jerusalem, and all were scattered here and there through the regions of Judea, except only the apostles.
God-fearing men came and took up Stephen, and they made great lamentation over him.
This Saul was doing great harm to the churches. He would enter houses and drag off men and women and hand them over to prison.
The apostles went about here and there and proclaimed the good news of the word of life.
Philip went down to the city of the Samaritans and preached Christ to them.
The people paid heed to the words he spoke to them, all together hearing them and seeing the signs that he was doing.
For those who had an unclean spirit, the spirits would cry out with a loud voice and come out. And many who were paralysed and lame were healed.
And there was great joy in that city.
There was a certain man named Simon who had previously been in that city practising sorcery and astonishing the people of the Samaritans, and he said of himself that he was someone great.
All of them, from the least to the greatest, paid heed to him and said, "This man is the power of God that is called Great."
They obeyed him, because for a long time he had astonished them with his sorceries.
And when they believed Philip's good news about the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, men and women were baptized.
And Simon himself also believed and was baptized, and he was in awe and followed Philip. As he saw the signs and the very great miracles that were happening, he was amazed.
So when the apostles who were in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.
When they arrived, they prayed for them, that the Holy Spirit might come upon them.
For until then the Holy Spirit had not yet come upon any of them; they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Then they laid their hands on them, and the Holy Spirit came upon them.
When Simon saw that the Holy Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles' hands, he offered them money
and said, "Give me this power too, so that whoever I lay my hands on may receive the Holy Spirit."
Peter said to him, "May your silver perish with you, because you think you can obtain the gift of God with money.
You have no part or inheritance in this matter, for your heart is not right before God.
So now repent of your wickedness and pray to the Lord, in the hope that the wickedness of the thoughts of your heart may be forgiven you,
for I see that you are in the bitterness of gall and in the bond of sin."
Simon answered and said, "Pray to the Lord for me, so that nothing of what you have said may come upon me."
They bore witness to the word and spoke the word of the Lord, then returned to Jerusalem, preaching the gospel in many other villages and cities of the Samaritans as well.
An angel of the Lord spoke to Philip and said, "Get up and go south, to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza. This is desert."

Philip got up at once and went. And behold, there was an Indian, a eunuch, a powerful official of Candace, queen of the Indians, who was in charge of all her treasure. He had come to Jerusalem to worship.
He was returning, sitting in his chariot and reading the prophet Isaiah.
The Holy Spirit said to Philip, "Go and join that chariot."
Philip went up and began to listen as he was reading the prophet Isaiah. He began to question him and said, "Do you understand what you are reading?"
He answered and said, "How can I understand unless someone guides me?" And he begged Philip to come up and sit with him in the chariot.
The passage of scripture he was reading was this: "Like a sheep he was given over to slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer, so he does not open his mouth.
In his humiliation his justice was taken away. Who will tell of his descendants? For his life is taken away from the earth."
The eunuch answered Philip and said, "I beg you, about whom does the prophet say this? About himself or about someone else?"
Philip opened his mouth and, starting from these scriptures, began to proclaim the good news of Jesus to him.
As they were going along the road, they came to some water, and the eunuch said, "Look, here is water. What now prevents me from being baptized?"
Philip said to him, "If you believe with all your heart, it is permitted." He answered and said to him, "I believe in the Son of God, Jesus Christ."
He ordered the chariot to stop, and both of them, Philip and the eunuch, went down into the water, and he baptized him.
When they came up out of the water, the Holy Spirit came upon the eunuch. The angel of the Lord carried Philip away, and the eunuch did not see him any more, and he went on his way rejoicing.
Philip was found in the region of Azotus. He went about there, preaching the gospel to all the cities until he came to Caesarea.
Saul was growing still more enraged and was full of anger and murder against the disciples of the Lord. He went to the high priest,

And he asked him for letters to Damascus, to the other synagogues, so that he might go there and, if he found any people of the way of this teaching, men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.
And as he was going, when he drew near to Damascus, suddenly a brightness of light from heaven was all around him.
And he fell to the ground and heard a voice, which said to him: "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? It is hard for you to kick against the goad."
He answered and said to him: "Who are you, Lord?" He said to him: "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
But get up and go into the city, and there you will be told what is right for you to do."
And the men who were with him stood amazed. They heard the voice, but they saw no one.
Saul got up from the ground. His eyes were open, but he saw nothing. Those who were with him took him by the hand and led him into Damascus.
And three days passed, and he saw nothing, and he neither ate nor drank.
There was a man there, one of the disciples, whose name was Ananias. And the Lord said to him in a vision: "Ananias!" And he said: "Here I am, Lord."
The Lord said to him: "Get up quickly and go to the quarter that is called Straight Street, and look in the house of Judas for Saul, who is called the man of Tarsus,
for look, he is praying there." And in a vision he had seen a man named Ananias come in and lay his hands on him, so that he might see again.
Ananias answered and said: "Lord, I have heard from many people about this man, how much evil he has done to your saints in Jerusalem,
and now he has come here too for this purpose, and he has received authority from the chief priests to carry off as prisoners all who call on your name."
The Lord said to him: "Go, for I am with you. I have found him to be a chosen vessel, to carry my name before all the Gentiles, kings and rulers, and the sons of Israel.
And I will show him how much suffering he must take upon himself for the sake of my name."

Ananias got up at once and went. He came and entered the house, laid his hands on him, and said: "Brother Saul, the Lord has sent me to you, Jesus, who appeared to you on the road by which you were coming, so that your eyes may see again and you may be filled with the Holy Spirit."
And immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he began to see. He got up and was baptized;
and he took food and was strengthened.
And he stayed there with the disciples in Damascus for some days, and at once he began to preach in the synagogues and to say: "This is Jesus, the Son of God."

All who heard him were amazed and said: "Is this not the man who was destroying those in Jerusalem who called on the name of Jesus? And he had come here too for that very purpose, so that he might bring as many as he found walking in this way bound to Jerusalem, to the chief priests.
But Saul grew stronger still, and he gathered all the Jews who lived in Damascus. He made the people understand and declared to them that this is the Christ.
When many days had passed, the Jews plotted to kill him.
And someone revealed this to Saul: they were watching the gates of the city night and day, so that they might somehow kill him.
And the brothers took him and let him down in a basket through a window in the wall.
And he went to Jerusalem, and there he tried to join the disciples, and they were all afraid of him; they did not believe that he was a disciple.

Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles, and told them how he had seen the Lord on the road, and that the Lord had spoken to him, and how in Damascus his name had been made known by the name of Jesus [?].
And he was with them, going in and out in Jerusalem, and he spoke openly in the name of the Lord.
He spoke and argued with the Greek-speakers, and they plotted to kill him.
When the brothers learned of this, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.
But the churches in all the regions of Judea, Galilee and Samaria were at peace, built up and made firm. They followed the fear of the Lord and grew strong through the comfort of the Holy Spirit.
And it came to pass that as Peter was travelling through all those places, he came down also to the saints who lived in Lydda.
And he found there a man whose name was Aeneas, who had been sick for eight years and lay bedridden on his bed, for he was paralysed.
Peter said to him, "Aeneas, the Lord Jesus Christ heals you; get up and throw off your bedding."
And at that very moment he immediately got up and stood upright, and all the inhabitants of Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
And there was in Joppa a woman disciple whose name was Tabitha, which in translation is called Gazelle. She was full of the good works and almsgiving that she did.
In those days she fell sick and died. They washed the dead woman, clothed her, carried her up and laid her in the upper room.
Since Lydda is near Joppa, when the disciples heard that Peter was there, they sent two men to him and told him, "Do not think it [?] to come to us."

Peter got up at once and went with them. When they arrived, they led him and brought him up into the upper room. And all the widows stood around him, weeping and showing him the tunics and all the garments that Tabitha had made while she was with them.

He had the whole crowd put out, and Peter knelt down and prayed. Then he turned to the body and said, "Tabitha, wake up in the name of Jesus Christ." And she immediately opened her eyes. When she saw Peter, she got up and sat.
He gave her his hand and raised her up, called the saints, the widows, and presented her to them alive.
All of Joppa came to know of it, and many believed in the Lord.
He stayed many days there in Joppa, with a man called Simon the tanner.
And there was a certain man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion of the cohort called the Italian,
devout and fearing the Lord together with all his household. He gave many alms among the people and prayed to God continually.
He clearly saw a vision at about the ninth hour of the day: an angel of the Lord came to him and said to him, "Cornelius!"
And he stared at him, was seized with terror and fear, and said, "Who are you, lord?" He said to him, "Your prayers and your alms have gone up as a memorial for you before the Lord.
"And now send men to Joppa and bring Simon, who is called Peter.
He is lodging with a certain Simon, a tanner, whose house is by the sea."
When the angel who had spoken to him had gone, he called two of his servants and a devout soldier, one of those who waited on him continually,
and he told them all this and sent them to Joppa.
On the next day, as they were on their way and coming near the city, Peter went up onto the roof to pray, at about the ninth hour.
He became hungry and wanted to eat. And while they were preparing food for him, a trance came over him;
and he saw the heavens opened, and an object like a great linen sheet, [let down] by its four corners from heaven to earth;
and in it were all the four-footed animals and creeping things of the earth and the birds of the sky.
And a voice came to Peter and said: "Get up, Peter, kill and eat."
Peter answered and said: "By no means, Lord, for nothing defiled or unclean has ever entered my mouth."
Then the voice came a second time and said to him: "What God has made clean, you must not consider defiled."
This happened three times, and the object was taken straight back up into heaven.
While Peter was puzzling in his heart over what the vision he had seen might mean, behold, the men who had come from Cornelius were asking for Simon's house, and they came and stood at his gate.
They called out [?] and asked: "Is it true that Simon, who is called Peter, is lodging here?"
And while Peter was still pondering the vision, the Holy Spirit said to him: "Behold, three men are standing outside looking for you;
get up, go down, and go with them, and do not doubt at all, for I have sent them to you."
Peter got up at once, went down to the men, and said: "Behold, I am the one you are looking for. Now what is the matter you have come about?"

They answered him: "Cornelius the centurion, a righteous and God-fearing man, who is well spoken of by the whole Jewish nation, received a command from an angel to bring you to his house and to hear words from you."
He invited the men in and had them stay there that day. The next day he got up and went with them, and some of the brothers who were in Joppa went along with him.
The day after that they entered Caesarea. Cornelius was waiting for him and had gathered his relatives and close friends.
And as Peter came in, Cornelius came out to meet him, fell at his feet, and worshipped him.
Peter raised him up and said: "Stand up, for I myself am only a man too."
And they talked together, and so they went inside, and he found a large gathering there.

Peter said to them: "You yourselves know that it is not lawful at all for a Jewish man to associate with Gentiles or to come into contact with foreigners. But God has commanded me that I should never regard anyone as foul or unclean.
That is why I came to you without objecting. Now I want to know why you sent for me."
And Cornelius said to him: "Four days ago, up to this very hour, I was praying my worship at the ninth hour in this house of mine, and a man in white clothing came and stood before me and said to me:
'Cornelius, your prayers and the alms of your good works have gone up as a memorial of you before God.
Now send to Joppa and summon Simon, who is called Peter. He is lodging in the house of a certain Simon, a tanner, by the seashore. He will come and speak to you.'
So I sent to you at once, and you have done well to come. Now, behold, we are all here before God to hear everything that the Lord has commanded you."
Peter opened his mouth and said: "Truly I know this: there is no partiality before God,
but in every nation whoever fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him.
As for the word that he sent to the sons of Israel, proclaiming the good news of peace through Jesus Christ: he himself is Lord of all.
You yourselves know the word that went throughout all Judea, which began from Galilee after the baptism that John preached:

about Jesus of Nazareth, whom the Lord anointed with the Holy Spirit and with power, who came and went about among us doing good and healing the sick, freeing those oppressed by the devil, for God was with him.
And we are witnesses of all the deeds he did in the land of Judea and in the city of Jerusalem. They killed him by hanging him on the tree;
but God raised him on the third day and caused him to be made manifest,
not to all the people, but to the disciples chosen beforehand by God, that is, to us, who ate and drank with him after his resurrection from the dead.
And he commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that he himself is the one chosen by God, the judge of the living and the dead.
To all this all the prophets bear witness: that through his name all who believe in him receive the forgiveness of sins."
While Peter was still saying this, the Holy Spirit came and rested on all who were hearing the word.
The believers from among the circumcised who had come in with Peter were amazed that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out on the Gentiles too,
for they heard them speaking in one tongue after another and glorifying God.

At that moment Peter answered and said: "Can anyone withhold the water so that these people may not be baptized, who are already filled with the Holy Spirit just as we are, who have believed this from the beginning?"
And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Then they begged him to stay with them for some days.
The apostles and the brothers who were in Judea heard that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out on the Gentiles too.
But when Peter came to Jerusalem, the brothers who were from among the circumcised kept away from him,
because he had gone in to uncircumcised men and eaten with them.
Then Peter began to explain it to them from the beginning, and said:

"I was in the city of Joppa, and while I was praying I saw an astonishing vision: a kind of vessel was coming down, like a great sheet, hanging from heaven by its four corners. It came down and reached right to me.
As I looked at it, I saw all the four-footed creatures and wild animals of the earth, the creeping things of the earth, and the birds of the sky.
And I heard the voice that said to me: 'Get up, Peter, kill and eat.'
And I said: 'Far be it from me, Lord, for nothing defiled or unclean has ever entered my mouth.'
A voice came from heaven and said: 'What God has made clean, you must not consider defiled.'
This happened three times, and then all of it was taken up into heaven.
And at that very moment three men arrived at the gate of the house where I was staying. They had been sent to me from Caesarea.
The Holy Spirit said to me: 'Get up and go with them without hesitation.' These brothers also came with me, and we went into the man's house.
He began to tell us how he had seen an angel standing in his house, who said to him: 'Send to Joppa and bring Simon, who is called Peter,
who will speak words to you by which you will be saved, you and all your household.'
And as I began to speak, the Holy Spirit came upon them, just as it had come upon us at the beginning.
And I remembered the word of the Lord, when he said: 'John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.'
So if God gave the same grace to the Gentiles as he gave to us at the beginning, when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, what power did I have to stand in God's way?"
When they heard this, they fell silent and glorified God, saying: "So God has seen fit to grant to the Gentiles too the repentance that leads to life."

Now the apostles, when they were scattered by the persecution that arose over Stephen, went off along the seacoast, some to Cyprus and some to Antioch. They spoke the word to no outsider, but only to the Jews.
Some of them were men from Cyprus and Cyrene, who came to Antioch and spoke to the Greek-speakers and preached the good news of the Lord Jesus.
And the hand of the Lord was with them to heal them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord.
News of this reached the ears of the people in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas to Antioch to deal with them.
He came and saw the grace of God and rejoiced, and he urged them all to stay true to the Lord with wholehearted devotion,
for he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And a great many people were added to the Lord.
Then he went off to Tarsus to look for Saul. He found him and brought him back, and they came to Antioch.
They spent a whole year there, gathering the church and teaching a great many people. It was in Antioch that the disciples were first called Christians.
In those days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of them, named Agabus, stood up and announced through the Holy Spirit that a severe famine was going to come over the whole world. This famine took place in the days of the emperor Claudius.
And the disciples, as each one was able, determined, every one of them, to send relief to the brothers who were living in Judea;
and this they did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas.
At that time King Herod laid hands on some of those of the church to do them harm,
and he killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.
When he saw that this was pleasing to the Jews, he went further and had Peter seized as well; and those were the days of Unleavened Bread.

And he seized him and put him in prison, and handed him over to four squads of four soldiers to guard him. He intended in his heart to bring him out after the days of the Passover and hand him over into the hands of the people.
So Peter was kept in that prison; but prayer was made earnestly by the churches to God for him.

Now when Herod was about to bring him out and hand him over into their hands, on that night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with double chains, and the guards of the prison were guarding the prison before the doors.

And an angel of the Lord came, and a great light shone in the building; he struck Peter on the side, woke him, and said to him: "Get up quickly." And the chains came apart and fell from his hands at once.
The angel said to him: "Put on your belt and put on your sandals"; and he did so. And he said: "Put on your garment and follow me."
And he went out and followed him, and he did not know that what was being done by the angel was real; he thought that he was seeing a vision.

When they had passed the first and the second guard, they came to the iron gate that led into the city, which opened for them by itself. When they had gone in, they passed along one street, and at once the angel left him.
And when Peter came to himself, he said in his mind: "Now I know truly that God has sent his angel and rescued me from the hands of Herod and from all that the Jewish people were expecting."
Having thought it over in his heart, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was called Mark, where many were gathered together and were praying.
When he knocked at the door of the gate, a maidservant named Rhoda came out to answer.
When she recognized Peter's voice, in her joy she did not open the door, but ran inside and told them: "Look, Peter is standing at the door."
They said to her: "You must be out of your mind." But she insisted all the more: "It is so." And they kept saying: "It must be his angel."
And Peter kept on knocking at the door. When they opened and saw him, they were amazed.

Then he motioned to them with his hand to be silent. Then he told them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison, and he instructed them: "Tell this to James and to the brothers." And he went away to another place.
And when day came, there was no small commotion among the soldiers: "What has become of Peter?"
Herod searched for him and did not find him. Then he questioned the guards and ordered them to be put to death. And Herod went down from Judea and stayed at Caesarea.

Herod was angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon. They came to him together and won over Aristakos [?], the head of the king's chamberlains, making him their friend. They asked for peace, because their country got its food from the king's land.
On an appointed day Herod put on royal robes, sat down on the throne and spoke to them.
All the people shouted with one voice, saying: "This is the voice of a god and not of men."
Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him down, because he did not give the glory to God. He was eaten by worms, and he breathed his last.
The word of God grew and spread.
When Barnabas and Saul had finished their service, they returned from Jerusalem to Antioch. They brought John with them, who was also called Mark.
In the church at Antioch there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas; Simeon, who was called Niger; Lucius of Cyrene; Manaen, who had been brought up with King Herod; and Saul.
While they were serving the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said: "Choose Barnabas and Saul and set them apart for me, for the work I have called them to do."
Then they prayed and fasted, laid their hands on them and sent them off.
After they were sent off, they went down to Seleucia, guided by the Holy Spirit. From there they boarded a ship and sailed to Cyprus.
From there they went on [?] to Salamis, and they began to preach the word of God in the synagogue of the Jews. They also had John with them as their helper.
When they had travelled through all the cities as far as Paphos, they met a man there named Bar-Jesus. He was a magician, a false prophet and a Jew.
He was an attendant of the proconsul Sergius Paulus, who was an intelligent man. The proconsul called Barnabas and Saul to him because he wanted to hear the word of God from them.
But Elymas the magician opposed them (this is what his name means). He tried to turn the proconsul away from the signs.
But Saul, who is Paul, was filled with the Holy Spirit. He looked straight at him
and said: "You are full of every kind of deceit and wickedness, you son of the devil and enemy of everything that is right! Will you not stop twisting the straight ways of the Lord?

Now the hand of the Lord is against you. You will be blind, and for a time you will not see the sun." At once mist and darkness fell over him, and he went around looking for someone to lead him by the hand.
When the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed, and he was amazed at the teaching about the Lord.
Paul and his companions left Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. But John left them there and went back to Jerusalem.
From Perga they went on to Antioch in Pisidia. On the Sabbath day they went into the synagogue and sat down.
After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the chief priests sent a message to them, saying: "Brothers, if you have a word of encouragement for the people, please speak."
Paul stood up, waved his hand for them to be quiet, and said: "Men of Israel, and you others here who fear God, listen to me.
The God of this people Israel chose our fathers and exalted the people during the time of their sojourn in the land of Egypt, and with a high arm he brought them out from there,
and for a period of forty years he nourished them in the wilderness.
And he destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan and gave them their land as an inheritance
for about four hundred and fifty years; and after this he gave them judges until the days of Samuel the prophet.
From then on they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul, the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for about forty years.

And when he had removed him, he raised up David to be king for them, to whom he himself bore witness and said: "I have found David, the son of Jesse, a man after my heart, who will do and fulfil all the will of my heart."
From this man's seed, according to the promise, God raised up for Israel the Saviour, Jesus,
before whose coming John the Baptist first preached a baptism of repentance to all Israel.
As John was completing his course, he said: "What you suppose me to be, I am not; but behold, one is coming after me, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie."
Men, brothers, children of the race of Abraham, and those among you who fear God: to you the word of this salvation has been sent.
For those who live in Jerusalem, and their rulers, did not know him, and, in accordance with the words of the prophets, which are read every Sabbath, they condemned him and fulfilled them.
They found no cause for death in him. Then they asked Pilate to have him killed.
When they had carried out everything that was written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.
But God raised him from the dead,
and for many days he appeared to those who had come up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are also his witnesses to the people.
And we bring you the good news of the gift that was promised to your fathers,
for God has fulfilled this for their children and has raised up Jesus for us, as it is written in the second psalm: "You are my Son; today I have begotten you."
And as for his raising him from the dead, never again to return to corruption, he said this: "I will give you the holy and sure blessings of David."
Therefore he also says in another place: "You will not let your Holy One see corruption."
For David, after he had served his own generation, fell asleep by the will of God, and was laid with his fathers and saw corruption.
But the one whom God raised up did not see corruption.
Let it be known to you, men, brothers, that through him the forgiveness of your sins is proclaimed to you, and from everything from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses,
everyone who believes in him is justified.
Beware, then, that what was spoken by the prophet does not come upon you:
"Look, you scoffers, and be amazed and perish, for I am doing a work in your days, a work that you will not believe even if someone tells it to you."
As they were about to leave, the people begged them to tell them this word of God again on the next Sabbath.
When the assembly had been dismissed, many of the Jews and of the believing proselytes followed them, Paul and Barnabas. They strengthened them and urged them to stand firm in the grace of God.
On the next Sabbath the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.
When the Jews saw so great a crowd, they were filled with envy. They rose up to argue against the words Paul had spoken, and they reviled them.

Barnabas and Paul spoke out boldly and said: "It was necessary for this word of God to be spoken to you first. But since you, behold, push it away and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we now turn to the Gentiles.
For this is what the Lord commanded us: 'I have set you as a light for the Gentiles, so that you may be a savior to the ends of the earth.'"
When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord. And as many as had been appointed to eternal life believed.
And the word of the Lord spread throughout all that region.
But the Jews stirred up the devout noble women and the leading men of the city. They started a persecution against Paul and Barnabas, threw them out of the city and drove them out of their territory.
But they shook the dust off their feet against them and went to the city of Iconium.
And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
In Iconium, as was the custom, we went into the synagogue of the Jews and spoke in such a way that a great multitude of Jews and Gentiles believed.
But the Jews who did not believe stirred up the hearts of the Gentiles and turned them against the brethren.
They stayed there a long time, speaking boldly in the Lord. He bore witness to their words of grace and granted that signs and wonders be done by their hands.
Then the people of the city were divided: some sided with the Jews and some with the apostles.
And when the Jews and the Gentiles, together with their rulers, plotted to attack them, abuse them and stone them,
they left that place and fled. They took refuge in the city of Lycaonia, in Lystra and Derbe, and in the surrounding villages,
and there they preached the gospel.
There was a man there in Lystra whose feet were weak. He had been lame from his mother's womb, and he sat there; he had never walked.
He heard the words that Paul was speaking. When Paul looked at him and saw that he had faith to be saved, he said to him in a loud voice:
"I tell you, O man, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: stand up straight on your feet." He sprang up and began to walk.
When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they raised their voices in the Lycaonian language and said: "The gods have taken the likeness of men and have come down to us."
They called Barnabas the god Zeus and Paul Hermes, because Paul was the leader in speaking.
Then the priest of the god Zeus, who was the chief of the city, brought bulls and garlands to the gates of the city with the crowd. He meant to offer a sacrifice.
When the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard this, they tore their clothes and rushed down to the people, crying out

and saying, "Men, why are you doing this? We too are only men, like you, and we bring you good news: that you should turn from these vain things to the living God, who made heaven and earth, the sea and everything that is in it."
In past generations he let all the nations walk in the ways of their own will,
and yet he did not leave his good works without witness at any time, giving you rain from heaven and seasons of harvest, filling your hearts with food and joy."
And when they had said this, they barely restrained the people from sacrificing to them, and made them go away, each to his own home.

And while they were still staying there and teaching, the Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium and spoke to them openly, and turned the people away from them. They said that they spoke nothing true but lied about everything. And they stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city. They supposed that he had died.
When the disciples came and gathered around him, he got up and went into the city, and on the next day he left with Barnabas, and they went to Derbe.
And they preached the gospel in that city and made many disciples, and they returned to Lystra, to Iconium, and to Antioch.
And they strengthened the hearts of the disciples and urged them to remain firm in the faith, saying, "Through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of God."
And by the laying on of hands they ordained elders for them in each church, and with prayer and fasting they commended them to the Lord in whom they had believed.
And when they had passed through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
And when they had spoken the word of God in Perga, they set out from there and came to Italy [?].
And from there they set out by ship and came to Antioch, from where they had been commended and strengthened by the grace of God for the work that they had completed.
And when they had arrived there, they gathered the congregation and told them all that God had done with them, and that he had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
And they stayed there no short time with the disciples.
And some came down from Judea and taught the brothers, saying to them, "Unless you are circumcised according to the law of Moses, you cannot be saved."

Since there was dissension and no small debate between Paul and Barnabas and them, it was arranged that Paul and Barnabas and some others of them should go up to Jerusalem, to the apostles and elders, about this dispute.
They were sent on their way by the congregation and passed through the coastal region and Samaria, telling them of the conversion of the Gentiles, and they brought great joy to all the brothers.
And when they arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the congregations, the apostles, and the elders, and they told them all that God had done with them.
But some who belonged to the party of the Pharisees and had become believers stood up and began to speak, saying, "They must be circumcised and commanded to keep the law of Moses."
The apostles and the elders gathered together to look into and consider this matter.

And when there had been much debate, Peter rose up and said to them: "Men, brothers, you yourselves know that from the first days God made it known among you that by my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of the gospel and believe.
And God, who knows the heart, bore witness to them, for he gave them the Holy Spirit, just as he did to us.
And he made no distinction between us and them, having cleansed their hearts by faith.
Now why do you test God by placing on the neck of the disciples a yoke which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
But we believe that we are saved through the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the same way as they are."
And the whole multitude fell silent and listened to Barnabas and Paul as they told how many miracles and signs God had done among the Gentiles by their hands.
And after they had fallen silent, James answered and said: "Men, brothers, listen to me:
Simeon has told you how God looked upon the Gentiles to take out from among them a people for his name;
and with this the words of the prophets agree, as it is written:
'After this I will return and rebuild the dwelling of David; what of it has fallen and been overthrown I will raise up, and I will rebuild it,
so that the rest of mankind may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles upon whom this my name is called, says the Lord, who has made
all this known from eternity.'
Therefore it seems right to me that we should not trouble those from among the Gentiles who have turned to God,
but that we should write to them that they keep away [?] from things sacrificed to idols, and from fornication, and from [?], and from blood;
for from the beginning, from ancient generations, Moses has had his preachers appointed in city after city, who read him aloud in the synagogues every sabbath."

Then it seemed right to the apostles and the elders, together with the whole assembly, to choose men from among them and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas, who was called Barsabbas, and Silas, men held in esteem among the brothers.
They wrote a letter by their hand as follows: "The apostles and the elders and the brothers, to you brothers from among the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and the region of Cilicia: greetings.

For we have heard that some from among us went out and stirred you up with words, unsettling [?] your hearts, telling you: 'Circumcision is required, and keeping the law of Moses.' We had given them no such command.
Now therefore it has seemed right to us, all the assemblies together, to choose these men and send them to you with Paul and Barnabas, our beloved,
men who have given up their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So we have sent Judas and Silas, and they too will tell you these things by word of mouth.
For it has seemed right to the Holy Spirit and to us that no greater burden be laid upon you except these things, which are the most necessary:
that you keep away from things sacrificed to idols, and from what is dead, and from eating blood, and from fornication. Keep yourselves from these things, do good, and live by the Lord."
When they had been sent off, they came to Antioch. And there they gathered the assembly and gave the letter into their hands.
When they had read the letter, they rejoiced greatly and took comfort in it.
Judas and Silas, since they themselves were also prophets, comforted the brethren with many words and strengthened them.
And they stayed there a long time, and they were sent off in peace by the brethren there to the apostles.
Silas decided to remain there.
But Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, and together with many others they taught and preached the words of the Lord.
Some days later Paul said to Barnabas: "Let us go back and visit the brethren in every city in which we preached the word of the Lord, and see how they are."
Barnabas wanted to take with them John, who was called Mark.
But Paul urged that they should not take with them the one who had left them the first time, in Pamphylia, and had not gone along with them in the work.
So there was a sharp disagreement between them, to the point that they parted from each other; and Barnabas took Mark with him and sailed away to Cyprus.
But Paul chose Silas and set out, committed by the brethren to the grace of God,
and he passed through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
He came to Derbe and Lystra. And there was a disciple there named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Gentile father,
who was well spoken of by the brethren of Lystra and Iconium.
Paul wanted him to go with him, so he took him and circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those places, for they all knew that his father was a Gentile.
And as they went through the cities, they taught them to keep the ordinances confirmed by the apostles and elders who were in Jerusalem.
So the churches were strengthened in the faith and increased in number day by day.
They went through Phrygia and the region of Galatia, and the Holy Spirit kept them from speaking the word in Asia.
When they came to Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of the Lord did not allow them.
So, passing by Mysia, they went down to Troas.
In a vision at night Paul saw a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him and saying: "Come over to Macedonia and help us."
When Paul had seen this vision, we immediately tried to leave for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us there to preach the gospel to them.
We set sail from Troas and ran a straight course to Samothrace, and the next day to Neapolis,
and from there to Philippi, which is the leading district of Macedonia, a city that is called a colony. We were in that city and stayed there some days.
On the Sabbath day we went outside the city to the riverbank, where we supposed prayer was offered; and we sat down and spoke to the women who had gathered there.
And a woman named Lydia was there, a seller of purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, a worshipper of God. She was listening, and the Lord opened her heart to heed the words spoken by Paul.
And when she was baptized, she and her household, she entreated us and said to us: "If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house and stay there." And she compelled us.
And it happened, as we were going to worship, that a slave girl met us who had a spirit of python, that is, of divination, and by her divination she brought her masters much profit.
She followed Paul and us, crying out and saying: "These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim to you the ways of life."

She did this for many days. Paul grew angry, turned to that evil spirit, and said: "I command you in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ to come out of her." And it came out of her at once, in that same hour.
When the woman's masters saw that the [?] of their profit had gone out of her, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers,
and they brought them and set them before the magistrates and said: "These men are stirring up this city of ours. They are Jews,
and they proclaim to us some law that it is not right for us to accept or to practice, for we are Romans."
And the crowd gathered against them, and the magistrates tore off their clothes and ordered them to be beaten with rods.
And after they had laid many blows on them, they threw them into prison and commanded the jailer to guard them securely.
When he received this command from them, he threw them into the inner prison and fastened their feet in the stocks.
Around midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.
Suddenly there was a great earthquake, and the prison was shaken to its foundations, and at once all the doors were opened and everyone's bonds were loosed.
And when the jailer suddenly woke up and saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, for he thought that all the prisoners had escaped.
Paul called to him with a loud voice and said: "Do yourself no harm, for we are all here."
He called for a light and went in there, and trembling seized him, and he fell at the knees of Paul and Silas.
He brought them outside and said: "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?"
They said to him: "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and all your house."
And they spoke the word of the Lord to him, and he believed, together with all his household.
And that same night the chief jailer took them and washed them of their wounds, and he himself was baptized, and all his household with him.
And he brought the apostles up and seated them [?] and set a table for them, and he rejoiced together with all his household, who had believed in the Lord.
And when it was day, the magistrates sent the officers and said: "Release those men whom we gave you as prisoners."
The chief jailer went in and told these words to Paul and Silas and said to them: "The magistrates have ordered your release. Now let us go in peace."

Paul said to him: "They beat us in public, blameless and innocent men, Roman men, and threw us into prison without cause, and now they have sent word to bring us out secretly? Not so; let them come themselves and bring us out of here."
The officers went and told the magistrates all this. When they heard it, fear came over them all the more, because they heard that those men were Romans.
They came quickly, brought them out of the prison, and begged them to leave and depart from their city.
When they came out of the prison, they went and entered Lydia's house. There they saw the brothers and comforted them, and then they left.
When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.
As Paul was accustomed, he went in to them, and on three Sabbaths he chose readings for them from the Scriptures,
explaining them and setting before them that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead, and that "This is the Christ whom I proclaim to you."
Some of them believed and joined Paul and Silas, and so did a great multitude of the God-fearing Gentiles and not a few of the leading women.
But the Jews became jealous. They brought some wicked men from the marketplace, formed a mob, and set the city in an uproar. They attacked Jason's house, seeking to bring them out before the people.
When they did not find them, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city rulers and cried out: "These men who have upset the whole world have come here,
and Jason has received them. All of them act against the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus."
With these words they stirred up the people and the city magistrates,
until they demanded a security from Jason, and only then did they let them go.
When the brothers came, they led them out that very night and sent Paul and Silas away toward Berea. When they came to that city, they went straight to the synagogue of the Jews.
These people were more noble than those of Thessalonica. They received the word with all eagerness and continually examined the Scriptures to see whether these things were so.
So many of them believed, and also some of the Gentiles, many women, and not a few men.
When the Jews of Thessalonica learned that Paul had proclaimed the word of God in Berea too, they came there as well and began to stir up the people.
The brothers immediately led Paul out and sent him away toward the seacoast, but Silas and Timothy stayed there.
Those who were escorting Paul brought him as far as Athens. They received a command from Paul for Silas and Timothy to come to him quickly, and they left.
While he was waiting in the city of Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he saw that the city was full of idolatry.
He spoke continually in the synagogue with the Jews and with the God-fearers, and every day in the streets with whoever happened to meet him.

Some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers argued with him. Some said, "What does this babbler want to say?" Others said, "This man [?] is a proclaimer of foreign demons," because he was preaching to them the resurrection of Jesus.
They took hold of him, brought him to the Areopagus and said: "May we know what this new teaching of the word that comes from you is?
You are bringing some strange things to our ears. We wish to know what this means."
Now all the Athenians, and the foreigners who had come there, spent their time on nothing else but telling or hearing something newer.
Then Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus and said: "Men of Athens, I see that in all things you are exceedingly given over to demons.
As I was walking around and looking at your objects of worship, I found an altar on which was written: 'An unknown god.' What you do not know and yet worship, this I proclaim to you.
God, who made the world and everything that is in it, is Lord of heaven and earth, and does not dwell in temples made by hands,
nor is he served by human hands, as though he needed anything, for he is the one who gives life and breath to all. And all
the races of men he made from one blood, to dwell on the whole face of the earth. He determined the appointed times and set the boundaries of their dwelling,
so that they would seek God. If anyone were to seek, he would find him, for he is not far from each one of us,
for through him we live, as some of your poets say: 'For we too are his offspring.'
Now if we are God's offspring, it is not fitting for us to think that the divine is like gold or silver or carbuncle, shaped by human craft and design.
For God overlooked those times of ignorance, and now he commands all people, at all times and in every place, to repent,
